question: A conducting rod of length $L$ and mass $m$ is pivoted at one end and rotates with a uniform angular velocity $\omega$ in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The other end of the rod slides on a circular conducting ring. A resistor $R$ is connected between the pivot and the ring. Neglecting gravity and friction, what is the external torque required to maintain the constant angular velocity $\omega$?
